reasons: spec.md's own determinism bullet for the new lesson_and_eval gate check states a specific failure contract -- the lesson file is found by the glob `lessons/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-<slug>.md`, and 'more than one match fails the check' (spec.md line ~101) -- but no test anywhere in plan.md exercises that path. Every other list of the check's fail cases (plan.md's 'Files that change' entry for checks.py, Order of work step 2, Risk 2's mitigation, and the Proof section's test_gate.py item, plus spec.md's own Acceptance bullet) enumerates exactly the same seven cases -- missing lesson, missing a required frontmatter field, prompt.md or checks.yaml missing, a failing index.py check, a dangling supersedes, a supersedes target whose status did not move to retired, an out-of-enum status -- and none of the four is 'two lesson files match the glob'. That is a distinct code path from 'missing lesson' (zero matches vs. two-or-more matches), so a test for 'missing lesson' does not exercise it. This project's own coding-standards skill (rule 4: 'every behavior change ships with a test that fails without it') is the rule plan.md itself invokes to justify its step-1 ordering; the plan does not meet that bar for this one stated behavior, so an implementer who works strictly from the plan's enumerated test list could ship the duplicate-match rule unimplemented or wrong and every planned test would still pass.
classification_reasons: The spec is now tight (every flagged concern closed with an explicit owner decision, the two prior review rounds' 37 combined items all verified applied in the current text), but blast radius is not small: a brand-new module (plugin/lessons/index.py), a new gate check registered in CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'], edits to two command files' allowed-tools and instructions, two template files, OPERATING_MODEL.md, and a two-manifest version bump, with plan.md's own Risk 2 naming the gate check as the step whose failure mode would silently stop enforcing the invariant rather than failing loudly.

None of the touched behavior is covered by any existing test: plugin/lessons/index.py and lesson_and_eval are new, so every test that proves them is also new and still to be written at phase (c); routine requires code the existing tests already cover, which does not hold here.
Both conditions above independently rule out routine regardless of the spec's tightness, per the build guide's three-way test (tight spec AND small blast radius AND existing coverage).
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome field-by-field against the current spec.md/plan.md; no scope drift introduced by this fix round, and the two carried-forward open questions (cross-project sharing, eval-case frontmatter) are still correctly left to their named owners rather than answered here.

Spec and plan: verified all 17 items of the owner's second 'Request changes' review (PR #124, review 5449795190, fix-requests.json) against the current text one by one -- the Flaky Test normalisation example, the index line's Tags: clause, the what-I-need indentation, the eval-case constants decided as non-imported duplicates in artifacts.py (not imported from case.py), the unified 'prompt.md or checks.yaml missing' wording everywhere, the newline/universal-newline/as_posix() requirement bullet, the Unsorted-does-not-fail-check sentence, --today under Acceptance, the finding.read_any wording, the allowed-tools Requirements bullet, one bullet per restored intent sentence, the full determinism write-up (heading order, file-name link, Mon-yyyy, no trailing period, Unsorted/Retired line shapes, (stale) placement), the explicit required-field list with retired_by correctly optional, the corrected glob, plugin/lessons/__init__.py in Order of work step 1, the phase-(f) unit test for the guard itself, and the HANDOFF.md/CHECKS_BY_PHASE/yamlish citation corrections -- all 17 are applied and consistent across every section that restates them, with no regression from the first round's 20 items. Found one genuine gap in the other direction: a behavior spec.md states explicitly (the glob's duplicate-match failure) has no matching entry in plan.md's otherwise exhaustive, four-times-repeated list of the new check's test cases (see reasons).

Proof: no code exists yet (phase b is design-only); this is the diff of spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml and the change folder's own evidence only; no toolchain log is expected or claimed for this phase, and none was cited for or against the diff. evidence/claude-b.json, claude-fix.json, gate-b.json, run-b.json and fix-response.md are prior rounds' runner/gate records (gate-b.json and fix-response.md are both still at HEAD 22ef512, the round-1 state, because /sdlc-fix step 6 writes fix-response.md and the gate re-runs only after this verdict) -- read for timeline context only, never cited as evidence about HEAD ac1ce30.

Blast radius: confirmed the diff (merge-base...HEAD) touches only changes/0003-.../{spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/*}; no file under .claude/**, this repository's own CLAUDE.md/REVIEW.md/sdlc.yaml, or any workflow template; status.yaml's phase/iterations fields are the change folder's own tracking data, not a guardrail file.

Policies: re-checked data-conventions rules 1 and 3 ('no risk_list item applies', 'no personal data') and coding-standards rule 4 against the plan's own test commitments -- the latter is where the gap above surfaced, since the plan's Order-of-work step 1 cites that exact rule as its own justification for the commit ordering, yet the plan does not itself satisfy it for one stated behavior.

The tests: cross-checked every behavior spec.md's determinism bullet lists for the new gate check against plan.md's four parallel test-case enumerations (Files-that-change/checks.py, Order of work step 2, Risk 2, Proof) and found they agree on six of seven listed items but omit a seventh behavior spec.md itself states (the duplicate-glob-match failure) -- tests as planned would pass whether or not that rule is implemented correctly. Change_type is 'feature', not 'fix', so the pre-existing-test-weakening rule does not apply, and no test file is touched in this diff anyway (phase b writes no tests).
